synthesis: The source supports a network of representation changes rather than one unconditional identity: integration by parts and parameter differentiation link weighted phase and log-modulus formulas while transporting explicit zero corrections; testing the zero-counting measure links weighted phase to sums over zero ordinates; and integrating the phase before applying a Littlewood relation links it to a horizontal log-modulus field. These bridges support the source's conditional identification of the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor criteria as differently written versions of a common zero-sensitive criterion. Pole cancellation supplies a related regularization-and-boundary-change example, but is not shown to be a step in that named-criterion chain.
source_support: Unit u07 derives an argument integral from Re(zeta'/zeta) by integration by parts and from a differentiated weighted log-modulus identity, then restores off-line-zero terms. Unit u11 writes arg zeta as the fluctuating term in N and uses Stieltjes integration to turn a kernel probe of dN into a zero-ordinate sum, recovering the Volchkov specialization. Unit u12 integrates arg zeta to S1 and uses a Littlewood relation to obtain nested horizontal log-modulus integrals. Unit u14 explicitly says the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor specializations are the same criterion differently written through a reproduced prior identity. Unit u09 independently cancels the pole with z-1 and relates vertical and real-axis log-modulus integrals using a principal value.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes three concrete bridges around the shared phase functional—b-differentiation plus integration by parts, testing the counting measure dN, and cumulative phase plus a Littlewood horizontal integral—while separating the independent pole-regularized boundary conversion from the named-criterion equivalence.
limits: The transformations require distinct branch conventions, boundary decay, differentiation under improper integrals, Stieltjes existence and boundary terms, interchange of nested improper integrals, and quoted prior theorems. The u09 relation is principal-value and figure-dependent, not established as a link in the Volchkov/BSY chain. OCR-fragmented formulas prevent certification of exact constants and kernels, and representational equivalence does not imply equal analytic or numerical tractability.
quality_reason: Accepted because u07, u11, u12, and u14 jointly establish concrete, mutually complementary transformations connecting phase, modulus, and zero statistics, yielding a relation unavailable from any one unit alone. The bounded synthesis removes the candidate's possible overstatement that pole cancellation participates in the same fully derived chain and preserves the conditional proof burdens.

synthesis: The source's criterion-construction recipe is constrained by the tractability of both the chosen contour kernel and every intermediate representation it creates. A kernel must support vanishing remote edges and computable contour contributions, while its off-line-zero correction must remain usable as an RH diagnostic; the two-scale example shows that a formally available integration-by-parts transfer can fail this test by replacing a rational weight with an analytically unmanageable logarithmic one.
source_support: Unit u04 exhibits the reusable rectangular-contour setup: a rational kernel, decay of the three remote edges, and evaluation by residues and generalized Littlewood methods, then transfers the target observable from log modulus to argument. Unit u08 shows the local obstruction: integrating the two-scale rational weight introduces log((d^2+t^2)/(c^2+t^2)) in a weighted log-modulus integral for which the authors see no route, so they retain direct contour analysis. Unit u16 abstracts the method as selecting g and evaluating the weighted log-zeta contour to construct RH criteria, while presenting practical decisiveness only as a hope.
nonparaphrase_operation: Intersects the general kernel-selection template with the concrete failed transfer: it treats decay, contour evaluation, and diagnostic zero contributions as simultaneous design obligations, and uses the logarithmic bridge object in u08 as a falsifying tractability check on an otherwise formal representation change.
limits: The source gives neither an admissible class or complete search over kernels nor an existence theorem for a practically decisive criterion. The u08 failure is the authors' bounded tractability assessment, not an impossibility proof for all indirect methods. Branch choices, convergence, singularity placement, exact residues, and noncancellation or identifiability of off-line-zero corrections remain case-specific proof burdens; formula details are OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because u04 and u16 establish the contour-design mechanism and aspiration, while u08 adds a specific obstruction that materially sharpens the recipe into a tractability-constrained search principle. The synthesis is not available from any parent alone and does not elevate the heuristic into evidence that a successful kernel exists.
